yarn.meaning: Every point and bullet survives: phishing, the three phishing tactics, the three protections, threats and gift-card demands, .gov check, typing the URL, upfront-fee grants, reporting profiles. "Hurry you up to click" softens "Urge" slightly.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "con punters", "makin' dodgy payments", "Check the message is fair dinkum", "Report shonky messages", "Shonks might ring you up", "Report suss profiles".
yarn.authenticity: Natural Aussie for the most part: "Scammers are always cookin' up brand-spankin'-new ways", "makin' out they're government officials". The dropped-g spelling is applied heavily ("usin' its official contact details", "double-check the spellin'").
yarn.register: Clearly Aussie throughout, but restrained for level 5: headings and many bullets stay plain ("Government agencies will never ask you to pay over the phone."). No swearing, which is allowed.
yarn.tone: Keeps the serious, protective consumer-warning tone under the slang.
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly, though the dropped g's clutter some lines: "Check the message is fair dinkum by gettin' in touch with the agency directly, usin' its official contact details."
yarn.variety: Varied: "punters", "dodgy", "fair dinkum", "shonky", "Shonks", "suss", "makin' out"; "dodgy" twice, and the g-dropping device leaned on.
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the Login.gov scam guide, structure intact.

engine.sense: Wrong-sense swap: "pressie cards" for gift cards; "trick punters" fits.

engine.register: Far under level 5: apart from "yer"/"ya", "punters", "brand-spankin'-new" and a few dropped g's, it is the original ("Verify the message by contacting the agency directly using official contact information.").
engine.tone: The warning tone survives because the text does.
engine.flow: Readable, but the "yer" spellings in formal sentences jar: "as well as methods to protect yerself".
engine.variety: Leans on "yer"/"ya" and dropped g's; little else.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives. "paying up for stuff that's a total rort" reframes "making fraudulent payments" a little; "will never, ever ask" adds emphasis to an existing claim.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact: "Dob in dodgy messages", "Shonks might ring up", "Sting you with fees", "cough up fees first", "suss profiles". "bodgy websites" strains: bodgy means shoddily made, whereas these fakes are built to look convincing.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian talking: "the most common dodges going around", "getting onto the agency directly", "Reckon there's some urgent drama with your benefits".
unharnessed.register: Full casual Aussie across headings' bodies and bullets alike, the right weight for level 5 in a guide; no swearing, which is allowed.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the protective warning tone; "never, ever" reinforces rather than jokes.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Don't go using search engines to find sign-in links. Type the official URL in yourself and double-check the spelling."
unharnessed.variety: Very varied: "rort", "dodges", "lingo", "Hassle", "drama", "legit", "Dob in", "Shonks", "bodgy", "Sting you", "cough up", "suss"; "Dob in" twice.
